rv.q: As Christmas traditions go, “Manual Cinema’s Christmas Carol” is a treasure.

Truly incredible on every level, Harris portrays a grieving widow and beginner puppeteer on the big screen while simultaneously operating as a vital part of the onstage puppeteering machine, grounding the production with warmth, humor, and emotional clarity.
Manual Cinema’s Christmas Carol is a beautiful, moving, redemptive work of art.

LaKecia Harris plays Aunt Trudy, lost in her moving boxes, ordering no contact Chinese, and trying to adhere to her now dead( from Covid 19) partner’s Christmas tradition of doing a puppet show of A Christmas Carol for the extended family. It has to be on Zoom, and Trudy is into her cups as she drags herself into Uncle Joe’s beloved show.
Manual Cinema’s artists have produced a large cast of beautifully painted puppets and paper scenery that evoke Victorian watercolor illustrations.
This production provides a space to journey through grief and joy, isolation and connection, regret and compassion.
The visual elements and the music, in addition to Harris's powerhouse performance, build in near-perfect harmony over the show's 80 minutes or so.

Manual Cinema’s reimagined production of A Christmas Carol confronts this head-on, and urges us to consider the true essence of Dickens’ message: the moral obligation to care for others and break the chains of indifference toward those who need our help.
For the adults in the room, it's a bracing, worthwhile plunge back into those dark, uncertain days we are all in such a hurry to leave behind.
It's an unforgettable and exhilarating holiday story.
This is a rare combination of quality theater with wonderful music and projections that in a special way form a movie of sorts...

cn.t: Manual Cinema's innovative shadow-puppet adaptation breathes fresh life into Dickens' classic by framing it through a pandemic widow's grief, earning praise for its beauty, emotional depth, and unique theatrical artistry.
